planSummary: Typed runtime conversion wave for EventLedger append/read behavior while preserving ASK source-run CLI compatibility.

slices.title: 001 EventLedger Runtime Parity Tests
slices.description: Add tests proving the current JS runtime and TypeScript-facing contract expectations stay aligned for append envelopes, defaults, ordering, and malformed NDJSON behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Tests cover sorted `readAll` and malformed NDJSON throw behavior.
Existing EventLedger guard tests continue to pass.

slices.title: 002 TypeScript EventLedger Runtime Helpers
slices.description: Add a TypeScript helper module for EventLedger event-envelope creation and event sorting without importing `.ts` from the source-run CLI path.
acceptanceCriteria: `ask-core/src/runtime/EventLedgerRuntime.ts` exports typed helper inputs/results using existing EventLedger contracts.
Helper fixtures or contract tests compile under `npm run typecheck`.
Helper behavior matches the JS runtime contract expectations.
No CLI/runtime loading path imports `.ts` directly.

slices.title: 003 Source Runtime Uses Shared Behavior
slices.description: Refactor `EventLedger.js` to use shared source-compatible behavior while preserving imports, SequenceStore behavior, append output, and readAll behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Existing imports of `EventLedger.js` continue to work.
`EventLedger.append()` returns the same public event envelope shape.
`EventLedger.readAll()` preserves sorted output and malformed NDJSON behavior.
Existing EventLedger, projection, and governance tests pass.

slices.title: 004 Migration Status Update
slices.description: Update TypeScript migration status to record EventLedger runtime compatibility conversion completion and identify the next safe migration area.
acceptanceCriteria: Docs mark `ask-ts-004` as runtime compatibility conversion complete for this wave.
Docs state full source-only `.ts` runtime loading remains deferred until CLI build/shim strategy is selected.
Docs name the next likely step as snapshot/runtime store boundary hardening or CLI build/shim strategy.
Docs preserve contracts-first, runtime-conversion-later, strictness-last framing.
